title: Six-class secp256k1 rho at 125.847878: lambda = R*e with all four batch products on shared rows, walk groups of 256, and exact plain-round fixed accounting

claims.statement: For a uniform full-production secp256k1 input Q=[x]P, the classical cold six-class negation-plus-GLV parallel Pollard-rho attack of proof.md and upstream-proof.md halts on every run with total work at most 2^125.847878 target-group-operation equivalents under classical-group-work-v2 (C=1000). It builds on bradcush's 886e6f54 (125.858271), whose walk, census, kappa, table, arrival rows and address rule it keeps, and changes how the batch inversion is spread over the passes: a forward loop prod forms e_i = acc_(i-1)*dy_i next to acc_i = acc_(i-1)*dx_i on acc_(i-1)'s shared rows, and pass 2 forms lambda_i = R*e_i next to R <- R*dx_i on R's shared rows, so all four batch products now run on shared rows at 72 instructions each (886e6f54 ran R*acc and R*dx on R's rows and acc*dx and lambda = dy*inv as plain 84-instruction products) and pass 2 no longer forms dy. The fused pass (loop A, both copies) runs the arrival, dx and dy. Per walk: loop A 52.5078125 (56.015625 in compare rounds, so compare rounds cost 3.5078125 + 380/2^20 more per walk, a hard row), prod 162.0078125, pass 2 339.5078125; step 554.0234375 + 26290/2^20 = 554.048510 instructions. Walk 0 is an ordinary slot (prod starts from acc = 1); the reserve is 336 milli-units per walk for at most 15 exits; the zero-test re-run is its own 2^19-unit action; a doubling is priced at step + 677. The declared run executes pass1, prod and pass2 on 267 production walks with 0 mismatches against big-integer affine secp256k1; both copies of loop A with 0 mismatches against big-integer dx and dy and the address rule; arrive.s with 0 mismatches against the bit-exact model and the exact rule; and all 3,855 + 1,028 exit stubs on constructed inputs with 0 mismatches against the Python limb ports and big-integer differences. kappa = 1.0001 follows from the shipped hazard census. Declared dependencies (proof.md section 6): 3655d7f0, 886e6f54, a00774d8, c06f6691, 4ac17b66, 445f9a1c, cbea87bf, 4c8222cc, 673640ef, 0a1c5772, 610c8e49, 6a6cb91c, 5f1ae3ce, 4595bad7, 01488655, 2bd168b5, daf2c741, a9297fb0, 807e4bf5, b5de673a, 02feb284. Recovery probability is greater than 0.39000019 and therefore at least 0.39 (failure rows 1.0103e-7 < 1.1e-7). Peak memory < 2^72 bytes; preprocessing capped at 2^59 units and included; no advice. Exact ledger: S_ops = 1.0001*S0 = 2^126.6995433, phase 1 = 2^125.847627, hard extras = 2^111.795749, random extras = 2^98.8451, allowance = 2^112.7543, W_ledger = 2^125.8478775 <= 1000*2^125.847878 milli-units; Markov ratio at most 0.0000647984 (exact, rounded up; the declared run's float ledger prints 0.0000648010) < 0.000065; certificate.py checks the claim and that 125.847877 fails, in exact arithmetic. No prior acceptance, review verdict or official score is a premise. This is an analytic heuristic bound, not a practical break.

experiments.purpose: Part A: production secp256k1 checks of the walk identities and the canonical-index rule; Part B: a scaled toy pipeline of the checkpoint-only walk (even-y key, per-trail phases, compares every 128th round) on subgroups of y^2=x^3+7 with node routing, a check that the old and the production compare rule reach the same endpoints, and an optional long-trail trap test (long_trails, not set in the declared run); kernels: Python limb ports of the field kernels against big integers, and the shipped loops (with rare exits on constructed inputs entering every stub), both copies of the fused pass (loop A: arrival, dx and dy), emitter wrappers and arrival rows executed by an AArch64 interpreter (kernels/a64.py) against affine secp256k1, a bit-exact model and the exact canonical rule, with instruction counts and the ledger recomputed. The toy run does not meter production instructions or implement 2^20 concurrent walks.
